note: Toripalimab, prolgolimab and pucotenlimab went into melanoma on human PD-1 knock-in mouse tumours, monkey occupancy and in-vitro saturation; the Chinese trials are acral/mucosal-dominant, which mutes response rates the mouse could not foresee, and the clean monkey package missed the immune-related harms.
label: Melanoma (anti-PD-1)

engagement.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: the monkey RO/PD work is Fu 2017 (doi:10.1038/aps.2016.161, abstract-level); the quoted FDA sentence is from the 26-week GLP study whose date the review does not give.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey (PD-1 receptor occupancy, PD-1+ T-cell PD)
engagement.note: Toripalimab binds only human and cynomolgus PD-1; monkeys showed saturated receptor occupancy and PD-1+ T-cell decreases, no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Monkey RO saturated, no patients yet
engagement.quote: That said, receptor occupancy was saturated in the 30 and 100 mg/kg dose groups during the dosing period, so that the target was fully exposed to the test article in a dose dependent manner during the dosing period.
engagement.judgement: Fu 2017 (Beijing Institute of Radiation Medicine/Junshi) is the published model paper: HBsAg-vaccinated monkeys given 1 and 10 mg/kg JS-001 showed dose-dependent falls in PD-1+ CD4/CD8 T cells backed by receptor occupancy. Mouse and rat PD-1 are not bound, so the monkey is the only engagement model.

engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral T-cell PD-1 receptor occupancy (full in both)
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey (PD-1 receptor occupancy, PD-1+ T-cell PD)
engagement.note: Phase 1 (22/36 melanoma, acral and mucosal) patients kept >80% PD-1 occupancy on blood T cells at 1-10 mg/kg Q2W, as monkeys had.
engagement.quote: As shown in Additional file 1 : Table S3, the majority of subjects in the 3 dose cohorts maintained full occupancy (> 80%) of the PD-1 receptor on the peripheral blood T lymphocytes over the course of treatment.
engagement.reason: Full PD-1 occupancy in patients as in monkeys
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Tang 2019 cites Fu 2017 ('promotes T cell activation in preclinical studies') but does not put monkey and patient RO side by side, so comparison_stated is false. Direct readout (receptor occupancy by flow). The phase 1 (NCT02836795, no results posted) mixed melanoma (61%) with urothelial and renal cancer; the occupancy readout is not tumour-specific, so the mixed population is accepted here. Magnitude is direction-only: both reached saturation, no quantitative threshold was carried across.

engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: Studies 34885_IVHU and TR003 are undated in the review; the clone-selection design (TAB001 clones 38 and 41 against nivolumab) places them before the 2016 phase 1. The circulating-cell null is 'data not shown'.
engagement.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
engagement.note: Toripalimab raised splenic CD3+/CD4+/CD8+ frequencies and effector-memory share in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice; circulating frequencies unchanged (data not shown). No patient comparison.
engagement.short: Splenic T-cell expansion in PBMC mice
engagement.quote: Treatment with toripalimab increased T cell numbers compared to isotype control (Figure 7, upper panel).
engagement.reason: Splenic readout has no patient counterpart
engagement.judgement: Opened as its own track per the checker's missing list: the review files two PBMC-engrafted NSG studies (34885_IVHU, TR003) that none of the draft's toripalimab tracks carries. The nearest patient PD readout is Tang 2019 (NCT02836795): 'There was no major impact of JS001 on the frequency of activated CD8+ T lymphocytes in the peripheral blood in individual subjects.' That agrees with the mouse's own circulating null (data not shown) but is an activation fraction in blood, not the lineage frequency in spleen the model reported, so it is not scored: not same (the headline splenic readout has no human counterpart) and not contra (the compartment the model reported unchanged was also unchanged in patients). A checker who takes the blood null as the comparison would score same at low confidence. Downstream tier: cell numbers, not occupancy.

engagement.confidence_note: Open-access full text (PMC7452040). The mice were Junshi's humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 strain, the same strain as the filed knock-in MC38 efficacy model, but the tracer, tumour (S180 sarcoma homograft) and readout (PET biodistribution) differ, so it is opened as its own track; the checker may fold it into tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse. The FDA review never mentions the PET work. Isotope superscripts are rendered inline in the quote (124I).
engagement.model: Humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 mouse with S180 homografts, 124I-toripalimab immuno-PET
engagement.note: 124I-labelled toripalimab accumulated in S180 tumours of humanised-PD-1 mice above IgG and cold-blocked controls; no human imaging yet.
engagement.short: Tracer uptake in hPD-1 mouse tumours
engagement.quote: Immuno-PET imaging showed that the uptake in the tumor area of the 124I-JS001 group at different time points was significantly higher than that of the blocking group or the 124I-hIgG group in the humanized PD1 mouse model.
engagement.judgement: A target-imaging system no draft track carries: clinical-grade 124I-toripalimab, validated in vitro on PHA-activated T cells, then imaged in humanised-PD-1 mice where tumour uptake exceeded the hIgG and cold-blocked groups. Direct tier (the labelled drug binding its target in vivo). Product in model: the tracer is toripalimab itself.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour uptake of 124I-toripalimab above background (mouse %ID/g vs patient SUVmax 0.2-4.7, not commensurable)
engagement.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only (Clin Nucl Med). Eight of 11 patients had melanoma; the readout is not tumour-type specific. In mice, cold antibody lowered tumour uptake; in patients a 5 mg cold co-injection raised tumour uptake by clearing the splenic sink, a dose-level difference, not a reversal. No ClinicalTrials.gov record found (queries 124I-JS001, toripalimab PET); ChiCTR not searched.
engagement.model: Humanised-PD-1 C57BL/6 mouse with S180 homografts, 124I-toripalimab immuno-PET
engagement.note: First-in-human 124I-toripalimab PET (8 melanoma, 3 urologic patients): every tumour lesion took up tracer, spleen high, as the humanised-PD-1 mouse showed.
engagement.short: Tracer uptake in all patient tumours
engagement.quote: All primary and metastatic tumor lesions in 11 patients demonstrated different levels of uptake of 124I-JS001 with SUVmax ranging from 0.2 to 4.7.
engagement.reason: Tumour tracer uptake translated to patients
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: the clinical abstract calls itself a 'pilot clinical translation' of the mouse work (same Peking group, Sheng and Yang on both) but gives no side-by-side numbers, so comparison_stated is false. The model's prediction, that the labelled antibody localises to PD-1-expressing tumour and lymphoid tissue, held in all 11 patients, with high splenic uptake as in mice. Direction only: mouse %ID/g and patient SUVmax are not commensurable, and the cold-antibody blocking ran the opposite way at the 5 mg human dose. Engagement, not efficacy: no uptake-versus-response comparison was made, so prediction_level stays class.

dose.confidence_note: Proxy opening year: the assay used circulating T cells from the phase 1 (2016-2017); the review gives no study date.
dose.model: Human T-cell PD-1 occupancy in vitro (saturation threshold)
dose.note: In vitro, >3 ug/mL toripalimab saturated PD-1 on human T cells; a 20 ug/mL trough target for tumour occupancy was set from it.
dose.quote: In vitro experiments demonstrated that when the serum/plasma concentration of toripalimab was >20 nM or 3 μg/mL, PD-1 receptors on the surface of T-cells were saturated.
dose.judgement: The dose model is not an animal: an in-vitro occupancy titration on phase-1 patient T cells, from which the sponsor derived a 20 ug/mL steady-state trough target (about 7x the saturating concentration) meant to cover the tumour microenvironment. The monkey NOAEL (100 mg/kg, 13-23x patient AUC) supplies the tolerability margin; it is scored on this track rather than opened as a separate dose track.

dose.magnitude_basis: steady-state trough (37.8 ug/mL at 3 mg/kg Q2W) vs the 20 ug/mL target
dose.model: Human T-cell PD-1 occupancy in vitro (saturation threshold)
dose.note: 3 mg/kg Q2W gave troughs of 38 ug/mL, above the 20 ug/mL target, with full occupancy; the same dose then carried POLARIS-01 and MELATORCH.
dose.quote: As shown in Additional file 1 : Table S3, the majority of subjects in the 3 dose cohorts maintained full occupancy (> 80%) of the PD-1 receptor on the peripheral blood T lymphocytes over the course of treatment.
dose.reason: Occupancy trough target reached and sufficient
dose.judgement: Tang 2019 states the comparison itself: steady-state troughs of 8.9, 37.8 and 174 ug/mL at 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg Q2W, 'indicating the PD-1 receptor will be fully occupied even at the lowest dose cohort'. 'Enough' is settled by POLARIS-01 (2020) at 3 mg/kg Q2W and MELATORCH (2026) at 240 mg Q2W, both at or above the 20 ug/mL target; the FDA reviewer notes responses in every exposure quartile and a flat exposure-safety relationship, so no higher dose was needed. margin_stated is true because the filed monkey package stated a NOAEL of 100 mg/kg (13-23x patient AUC) and patients were dosed to target without that toxicity (decision 16). No MTD was reached clinically. The within_2x call is on trough versus target; the dose is really set by occupancy, not exposure-response, which the label says is 'not fully characterized'.

efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy opening year: Study TR003 is undated in the review; the drug entered patients in March 2016 and its preclinical package was published in 2017.
efficacy.model: Human PD-1 knock-in mouse bearing MC38 tumours
efficacy.note: Toripalimab slowed MC38 growth in human PD-1 knock-in mice at >=1 mg/kg twice weekly; no melanoma model and no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: hPD-1 knock-in mice: MC38 growth slowed
efficacy.quote: Administration of toripalimab to MC38-bearing KI mice i.p. twice weekly at 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg resulted in treatment-related decreased tumor growth at doses ≥ 1 mg/kg (Figure 9).
efficacy.judgement: The efficacy model is a colon-carcinoma syngeneic line in PD-1-humanised C57BL/6 mice, not a melanoma model; a second system (NSG mice with MC38 plus allogeneic CD8 T cells raised against 624Mel melanoma cells) showed only minor activity and is not opened as a track. Prediction is class-level (anti-PD-1 works) with nothing about tumour type or subtype.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MC38 tumour growth inhibition vs RECIST objective response rate (different metrics)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Tang 2020 (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled); the subtype ORRs are from the open-access five-year follow-up (doi:10.1093/oncolo/oyae045).
efficacy.model: Human PD-1 knock-in mouse bearing MC38 tumours
efficacy.note: POLARIS-01 (128 Chinese patients, 50 acral, 22 mucosal) met its ORR primary: 17.3%, durable, PD-L1-enriched; below cutaneous-melanoma anti-PD-1 rates.
efficacy.quote: Among 127 patients assessed, 1 complete response, 21 partial response, and 51 stable disease were observed for objective response rate of 17.3% and disease control rate of 57.5%.

patient_trials.quote: The primary objective was safety and objective response rate.

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: no source puts the knock-in mouse beside the trial. POLARIS-01 is single-arm with ORR as primary; China granted conditional approval on it in December 2018, before publication, which is why 2020 (epub 22 April 2020) is the earliest public comparison. Direction matched but the magnitude is muted: ORR 14% in acral, 0% in mucosal, 31% in non-acral cutaneous, against 28-40% in cutaneous-dominant Western anti-PD-1 trials. The mouse model carries no acral or mucosal biology, so it could not have predicted that gradient; the subtype mix, not the model, explains the gap, and the status stays same with direction_only. Prolgolimab's MIRACULUM (NCT03269565, Tjulandin 2021, cutaneous-dominant Russian cohort, ORR 38.1%/28.6%, primary met) and pucotenlimab's phase 2 (NCT04749485, Cui 2023, 52% acral/19% mucosal, ORR 20.2%) are consistent but have no published pre-clinic model, so they do not sit on this track. Nivolumab and pembrolizumab are the class context, not members, and are not scored.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: CT26 tumour growth inhibition vs MIRACULUM objective response rate
efficacy.confidence_note: BIOCAD-authored; the human side is cited as known ('has demonstrated high efficacy in patients with metastatic melanoma'), not re-analysed; the pembrolizumab-vs-prolgolimab ranking has no clinical head-to-head.
efficacy.model: Human PD-1 knock-in BALB/c mouse bearing CT26 tumours (prolgolimab vs pembrolizumab)
efficacy.note: Built after prolgolimab's Russian approval: in hPD-1 knock-in mice, prolgolimab inhibited CT26 growth 56% vs 16% for pembrolizumab; melanoma efficacy already known.
efficacy.quote: An in vivo study in mice inoculated with CT26.wt cancer cells showed that tumor growth inhibition was 16% for pembrolizumab and 56% for prolgolimab.

patient_trials.quote: The MIRACULUM study met its primary end-point in both the study arms.

efficacy.judgement: Separate track under this run's identity rule: a different model (BALB/c hPD-1/hGITR knock-in, CT26 colon line) making a different prediction (IgG1-LALA prolgolimab outperforms IgG4 anti-PD-1) from the toripalimab MC38 system. It was published in October 2024, after MIRACULUM (2021) and the 2020 Russian approval, so it is a retrodiction and can only be retro or contra; it reproduces the known class activity, hence retro. Whatever model BIOCAD filed before the clinic is unpublished and could not be verified. The sponsor's own claim of superiority over pembrolizumab is untested in patients and does not change the status.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MC38 tumour growth inhibition vs PFS hazard ratio
efficacy.model: Human PD-1 knock-in mouse bearing MC38 tumours
efficacy.note: MELATORCH, first randomised phase 3 for a member: toripalimab beat dacarbazine on BICR PFS (HR 0.71) in a 63% acral cohort; ORR only 11%.
efficacy.quote: Toripalimab significantly reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 29.2% (hazard ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.53-0.95; P = .02) compared with dacarbazine as assessed by BICR.

patient_trials.quote: Progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, version 1.1.

efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2020 call with a randomised primary endpoint (NCT03430297, completed July 2023, no registry results posted; published JAMA Oncology March 2026). The effect is real but small (ORR 11.0% vs 8.6%), again in a predominantly acral population; a cutaneous-melanoma trial of a member has not been run against chemotherapy. Abstract-level reading.

efficacy.confidence_note: Year is a proxy as in the engagement cell; Study TR003 is undated in the review and the reviewer gives no tumour growth inhibition number, only 'minor antitumor activity'.
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: In Study TR003, toripalimab had minor antitumor activity against MC38 in NSG mice engrafted with allogeneic anti-624Mel CD8 CTLs; no melanoma tumour, no patient comparison.
efficacy.short: Minor MC38 activity with allogeneic CTLs
efficacy.quote: Engraftment of T cells alone had no antitumor activity and toripalimab (10 mg i.p. twice weekly) had minor antitumor activity in T cell-engrafted mice harboring allogeneic T cells (Figure 8).
efficacy.judgement: The filed efficacy arm of this system is odd: a mouse colon tumour (MC38) in NSG mice given allogeneic human CD8 CTLs raised against B7-1-transfected 624Mel melanoma cells, so the T cells were not tumour-specific and the effect was minor. Nobody had compared it with patients at this date; toripalimab's own melanoma comparison in the draft sits on the knock-in MC38 track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: qualitative 'minor antitumor activity' of toripalimab in MC38/allogeneic-CTL NSG mice vs RECIST objective response rate 17.3%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Tang 2020 (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled; quote confirmed verbatim by the checker on the draft's entry). The model side is qualitative ('minor antitumor activity', no TGI number) in a non-melanoma tumour with non-specific allogeneic T cells, so the pairing is weak. NCT03013101 has no posted results.
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: POLARIS-01 met its ORR primary (17.3%, 128 Chinese patients, acral/mucosal-heavy); the allogeneic-CTL NSG arm had predicted only minor toripalimab activity.
efficacy.short: Modest ORR after minor mouse activity
efficacy.quote: Among 127 patients assessed, 1 complete response, 21 partial response, and 51 stable disease were observed for objective response rate of 17.3% and disease control rate of 57.5%.

patient_trials.quote: The primary objective was safety and objective response rate.

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: no source puts the T-cell-engrafted NSG study beside POLARIS-01. The model made a weak positive prediction for toripalimab and the single-arm ORR primary was met (China conditional approval December 2018, publication April 2020 is the earliest public comparison), so direction agreed and the muted magnitude is of a piece with 'minor'. Scored same at low confidence rather than left untested because the brief scores any directional agreement; a checker who regards the allogeneic-CTL arm as too far from a melanoma prediction would keep this cell untested until the 2023 pucotenlimab entry.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HCC827 xenograft tumour growth inhibition in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice vs RECIST objective response rate 20.17% (different metrics)
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text for both papers (PMC7153830, PMC9901108). The MiXeno tumour was a lung adenocarcinoma xenograft (HCC827), not melanoma. No NMPA review is public, so whether the model was filed is unknown. The mAbs DOI resolves (tandfonline returns 403 to scripted requests; confirmed through PMC).
efficacy.model: Human PBMC/T-cell-engrafted NSG mouse (T-cell expansion; MC38 and HCC827 grafts)
efficacy.note: Pucotenlimab (HX008) inhibited HCC827 growth in PBMC-engrafted NSG mice (Zhang 2020); its melanoma phase 2 (119 patients, 52% acral) met its ORR primary at 20.2%.
efficacy.quote: As the lower limit of the 95% CI of actual ORR exceeded the threshold of 10%, the primary endpoint of this study was reached.

patient_trials.quote: The primary endpoint was ORR assessed by IRC based on RECIST v1.1.

efficacy.reason: HX008 MiXeno activity; melanoma ORR primary met
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Cui 2023 never mentions the mouse work, and Zhang 2020 (mAbs) predates the melanoma result (trial start 2018-11-08; ORR first public with the 2023 paper; registry record posted 2021-02-11, no results posted), so this is a prospective prediction, not a retrodiction. The draft's efficacy judgement says pucotenlimab 'has no published pre-clinic model'; Zhang 2020 is that model: 'In both models, HX008 significantly inhibits tumor growth and shows an effective antitumor response comparable to approved anti-PD-1 drugs.' Only the PBMC MiXeno arm is this system; the HuGEMM human-PD-1 knock-in MC38 arm is the same system as the draft's tori-hpd1-knockin-mc38-mouse track and is listed under considered_not_added. Second member drug on the track, hence strengthens. Direction only: TGI in a lung xenograft against melanoma ORR, and the subtype gradient (cutaneous 36%, acral 16%, mucosal 9%) is nothing the model carried.

safety.confidence_note: Proxy opening year; the review does not date the GLP studies, which precede the 2016 first-in-human dosing.
safety.note: 26-week monkey study at up to 100 mg/kg (13-23x patient AUC) found no toxicity, including hormone and immune-function panels; no patient data yet.
safety.quote: All other monkeys survived the duration of the study with no findings of toxicity in any parameter measured.
safety.judgement: The package affirmatively predicted no toxicity rather than being silent: histopathology, thyroid/hormone analysis and immunophenotyping were all unremarkable, with minimal inflammatory infiltrates in treated and control animals alike.

safety.confidence_note: Mixed-tumour phase 1 (22 melanoma of 36); the melanoma-only irAE profile is confirmed by POLARIS-01 and its five-year follow-up (next entry).
safety.note: Phase 1 patients (61% melanoma) had immune-related thyroid events; 100% had treatment-related AEs, 36% grade >=3. Monkeys with full occupancy showed none.
safety.short: Thyroid irAEs the monkey never showed
safety.quote: Observed irAEs included two hypothyroidisms (one grade 1 and one grade 2) and one hyperthyroidism (grade 1).
safety.judgement: Scored contra because the species could have shown the harm: thyroiditis, hepatitis, colitis and dermatitis are histologically visible in a monkey, hormone panels were run, and the package reported nothing at exposures 13-23x the clinical AUC with saturated occupancy. A reading that treats irAEs as expected class pharmacology outside the tox model's remit would score untested; I did not take it, because the review relied on the clean monkey package as the safety prediction. Paired by me; the FDA review makes no nonclinical-clinical irAE correlation. Not scored: the macaque tuberculosis exacerbation (Kauffman 2021) and the murine pregnancy findings, which the label carries as class warnings but which are retrodictive literature, not this product's model.

safety.confidence_note: Open-access full text read; percentages are shares of long-term irAEs, not patient incidences.
safety.note: POLARIS-01 five-year follow-up: endocrine (36%) and skin (32%) irAEs dominated long-term toxicity in melanoma; grade >=3 TRAEs 19.5%.
safety.short: Endocrine and skin irAEs in melanoma cohort
safety.quote: Endocrine-related (36.0%) and skin-related (32.4%) AEs were the majority of long-term irAEs involving immunotherapy.
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2019 call in a melanoma-only cohort (NCT03013101, no registry results). Pucotenlimab's melanoma phase 2 (Cui 2023, doi:10.1186/s12885-022-10473-y) reports irAEs in 47.9% of patients, hypothyroidism 12.6% and skin depigmentation 21.0%, and MELATORCH grade >=3 TRAEs in 28.3%, the same picture for other members; their monkey packages are unpublished so they are not scored on this track. No member showed a harm in monkeys that failed to appear in patients, so there is no opposite-direction miss.
